To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an iterative algorithm for computing lower and upper bounds for the distance to the classification decision boundary of a ReLU network, and that our method is efficient and provides competitive or better results than existing approaches.

(i) we propose an efficient bi-directional verification algorithm that computes a lower bound and an upper bound on the distance to the boundary of ReLU networks; (ii) we show that the upper bound can be used to measure the quality of the certificate; (iii) our approach is competitive to the current state-of-the-art methods for the verification problem.

1) we propose a novel method that efficiently computes a robustness certificate for a NN classifier around a given input; 2) our method is competitive with the current state of the art and provides better results in most of the cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How can we measure the robustness of a neural network classifier? (2) What can be the role of convex optimization in this context? We believe that our approach provides a solid foundation for future research in this area.

two main aspects: (i) we present an efficient method for computing the distance to decision boundaries in ReLU networks and (ii) we show how this method can be used to compute robustness certificates for deep neural networks.

our approach is competitive in terms of the quality of the obtained certificates.

we present a method that is efficient, provides certificates, can be used to verify a large range of networks and is applicable to both, binary and multi-class classification.

a single convex QP is enough to provide a certificate of robustness around a given sample and can be used to efficiently verify the robustness of ReLU networks.
